olivia (customer): Hey team — we started getting errors from the embeddings endpoint after a rollout yesterday. ~30% of requests return a 400 with `dimension mismatch` and others are slow (p95 ~1.2s, used to be ~200ms). This is impacting our search freshness. attaching a failing payload below.

olivia (customer): curl reproducer: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"open-vec-2.0","input":["docA","docB"],"batch_size":8}'
```

olivia (customer): Response we see (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but received 1024 for item 1"}
```

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this — we'll triage. Do you have the full request headers + the trace id if available? Also, is this started after any model change on your side?

olivia (customer): We didn't change anything client-side. We did flip `prefer_low_cost` on yesterday but that's a lightweight flag. I don't see trace ids in our response. Example request id header from response is `x-request-id: rw-req-9a2f`.

maria (support): thanks — can you confirm whether you pin model versions? you passed `open-vec-2.0` which has two runtime variants (fp16-1536 and quant-1024) and the routing policy might pick a cheaper variant when load spikes. trying to reproduce now.

ingest-bot: Deploy to inference-fleet stage-3 succeeded at 2026-06-14T03:12:05Z (sha: fc9a7).

maria (support): david, can you take a look? suspect routing fallback -> model variant mismatch during batching (mixed-dim batch).

david (sre): on it. quick notes: mixed-dimension error arises when a batch includes requests routed to different model artifacts (1536 vs 1024) but the runtime assumes uniform output dim per batch. two suspicious causes: 1) routing policy recently changed to bin by cost tier, 2) autoscaler stretched across hosts with different cached model variants. grabbing logs.

neil (observability): if you have the `x-request-id` or `x-redwood-trace` we can pull span breakdown. You can also toggle per-request tracing in Console -> Requests -> enable `trace_on` for that api key to capture full spans.

olivia (customer): We have `x-request-id: rw-req-9a2f` and a short trace header `x-redwood-trace: rw-abcdef1234` returned on one failed call.

neil (observability): pulled trace rw-abcdef1234. Span summary (ordered):
- ingress.accept  -> queue_ms: 12
- route.select   -> route_lookup_ms: 34
- batch.assemble  -> batching_wait_ms: 410
- model.compute  -> model_compute_ms: 118
- response.serialize -> serialize_ms: 8
- egress.send -> network_ms: 5
Total observed server-side: ~587ms (client-reported p95 higher due to client queue + network). Important: batch.assemble has high wait and model.compute spans show inconsistent `output_dim` metadata between items in same batch (1536 vs 1024).

neil (observability): grabbing the batch-assembly logs for the same trace:
```
[2026-06-14T03:18:21Z] batch_id=bb-779 queue_time_ms=412 items=8 variants=[open-vec-2.0:fp16-1536, open-vec-2.0:quant-1024] error=dim_mismatch
```

maria (support): that matches the customer's 400. Suggested root cause so far: routing/fallback is sometimes selecting a quantized variant with different embedding size, and batching then fails when both variants end up in same batch.

olivia (customer): Is there a quick mitigation? We need search working ASAP.

david (sre): Immediate mitigations: 1) set `batch_size=1` on the client to avoid cross-variant batched mixes (temp fix), 2) add `model_variant=fp16-1536` as an explicit param or pin model version (recommended), 3) disable `prefer_low_cost` routing for your key while we fix routing rules. We'll push a hotfix to reject cross-variant mixing at batch-assembly time with clearer logs.

maria (support): Can you try `batch_size:1` and echo results? Also, I can update a policy to keep your requests on the 1536 variant until the fix is rolled.

olivia (customer): Switching to batch_size=1 reduced the 400s to ~0% and p95 improved to ~250ms. thanks. We'll keep that while you patch.

neil (observability): root cause follow-up plan:
- short-term: prevent mixed-variant batch assembly in runtime (reject/break into per-variant batches).
- mid-term: add model-compatibility check and a Console alert when variant dim changes are detected for a model id.
- long-term: routing policy update so variant selection is stable per-api-key (sticky per minute) and model catalog explicitly exposes embedding_dim as a routing constraint.

maria (support): i've created a ticket and flagged priority P1: RW-ISSUE-2026-468. david/infra will post a patch for batch assembly change.

david (sre): patch: runtime now checks artifact.embedding_dim on batch assemble and splits batches when mismatch found. rolling to canary for 10% ingestion nodes. rollback if we see perf regression.

ingest-bot: Rollout started: canary 10% (inference-fleet).

neil (observability): For your dashboards, to help track this we added a panel in Console > Dashboards > Embeddings -> \"per-request embedding_dim consistency\" which surfaces mismatched-batch count and % of batches with mixed dims. You can also use the raw metric `embed.batch.mixed_dim_count` and the trace tag `embed.output_dim` in tracing queries.

olivia (customer): Thanks — after canary went live we saw zero dim_mismatch 400s in our traffic for the next 45m. Please let us know when the full rollout is done. Any postmortem or follow-up actions we should expect?

maria (support): we'll keep you posted. Postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and a recommended client-side best practice doc (pinning or explicit model_variant). Also we'll add a small note to the API docs about `embedding_dim` incompatibility when using routing that can pick variants.

david (sre): Full rollout planned in 2 hours after canary health checks. Post-roll we'll backfill metrics and send PM with steps.

neil (observability): If you want to run an automated audit across your historical requests we can run a job to scan last 72h for any `embed.output_dim` variance per model id and share a CSV. Let me know and i'll queue.

olivia (customer): yes please run the audit and share the CSV — would like to confirm nothing slipped through earlier. appreciate the fast help. :raised_hands:

maria (support): assigning RW-ISSUE-2026-468 -> david/neil. I'll keep this thread updated and attach the postmortem when ready. :lock:
